screening_results.reason: This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 24–37; N=10 for fMRI) using socially relevant non-verbal vocalizations and animated faces, addressing social-related perception/understanding of others. Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, maps transformed to Talairach space, thresholded maps and ROI analyses) are presented as group activation maps (figures/tables), satisfying group whole-brain voxelwise reporting (not merely ROI-based). Healthy adult results are reported separately and clearly. Although slice coverage was focused on temporal cortex, the paper presents group voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy sample, meeting the review’s requirements.

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production tied to social communication and empathy (social-related processing). Sample: 19 healthy, right-handed native-English adults aged 18–58 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) thresholded and corrected (p<0.05 FDR, cluster k>5) and describes coordinates and supplementary materials; overlap/SVC and whole-brain contrasts are reported in text and figures. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI during social tasks in healthy adults (theory-of-mind and social attribution-of-attention) and meets I3 and I4. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy group. Task-related analyses were performed using localized ICA within a TPJ ROI (ROI-limited task decomposition) and task relevance was assessed via IC time-course regressions; whole-brain results are limited to seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E3.

The study uses task fMRI during a social-related face encoding/recognition paradigm (meets I3) and includes healthy adult participants (young subgroup aged 20–31; meets I4). However, the imaging analyses reported are region-of-interest (amygdala) extractions and parameter estimates; the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain results for the healthy group. Because no unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy group is provided, the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using an explicit social task (imitate/observe emotional faces) probing perception/understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group-level analyses (PLS and GLM) with voxelwise brain maps rendered in MNI space and thresholded voxel patterns reported, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Healthy participant results are reported for the group (neuroimaging data from 20 participants used for final analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level task activation data.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that involves perception and understanding of others’ emotions. The sample comprises healthy adults (final fMRI sample N=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects paired t-tests, TFCE FWE-corrected results) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI whole-brain task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, combined N=59) performing social-related semantic tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant words), satisfying the review’s social-processing target. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and peak coordinates presented, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control participants; ROI analyses are supplementary. Study 2 includes control participants reported separately from patient data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of interactive joint-action (leading vs following) that probes social cognitive processes (mentalizing, perception of others) during a social task. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean ages ~40) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, Following>Leading, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and whole-brain regression analyses; results are presented for the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social perception (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified for the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to be across all participants or focus on group contrasts (BPD vs controls) and ROI analyses for the amygdala are reported for controls. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a clear, group-level whole-brain healthy/control task map; that requirement is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts or pooled analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a socioemotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces) during functional MRI, addressing social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises 49 healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) with results reported for this healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (F > N, N > F) using whole-brain TFCE/FWE-corrected analyses, including coordinates, figures, and descriptions in the text (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) probing social exclusion/affiliation processes in healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates (including clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction) and provides coordinate tables and described contrasts for the healthy/control sample. All required inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in healthy adults are met, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (visual processing of dyadic interactions), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain preprocessing and GLM estimation to generate run-wise whole-brain beta maps and report group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests) and whole-brain searchlight analyses. Results include group-level voxelwise classification/searchlight findings and discussion of whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses/maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or resting-state-only) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social neuroeconomic task (prisoners' dilemma) probing social behaviour and cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; ages 18–50) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the control group (one-sample t-tests and per-group analyses with whole-brain results described and visualized; thresholding and cluster reporting are provided), satisfying the requirement for unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. Constructs assessed (trust/cooperation, mentalizing, face trustworthiness) fall within social-related processing. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (dynamic facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group (TD). The reported whole-brain analyses focus on between-group comparisons and found no significant additional activations; the main task results are given as ROI/MANCOVA analyses and DCM (effective connectivity). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception focusing on eye gaze (a social signal) and identity, involving healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24). The tasks probe social communication/perception of others (gaze direction). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-based results (z>4, clusters and Talairach/SPM coordinates) for the healthy sample, satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are adults).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion: I3 met — study used fMRI during a social-related task (perception of racial ingroup/outgroup faces). Inclusion not verifiable: I4 (sample age/healthy adult status not reported in provided text), I5 (no clear report of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map in the provided content; the abstract emphasizes amygdala responses and ROI analyses). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be conclusively applied from the abstract alone. Because core information needed to confirm all inclusion criteria (especially I4 and I5) is missing, I exclude this record pending full-text availability.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI social task with ten volunteers, so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants) are likely met. However I5 (reporting of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task map) cannot be verified from the provided content. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending retrieval of the complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E2-E6) are clearly met based on the available information.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of trustworthiness judgments (a social-evaluative task) in healthy adult participants (final N=14, ages 18–30). It includes group-level (random-effects) voxelwise analyses and reports whole-brain statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables for task effects (main effect of trustworthiness and task × trustworthiness contrasts), with small-volume corrections but also whole-brain reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (causal attributions, self vs other, self-serving bias) using task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults. Sample: 12 neurologically healthy right-handed male volunteers (age range 20–51) — meets the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects and supplemental random-effects ROI tests), with thresholded statistical maps, tables of peak coordinates, and figures showing activations (e.g., premotor cortex, cerebellum, STS, bilateral caudate) — satisfying whole-brain reporting and coordinate/tabular results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social processing (learning moral status of faces via a Prisoner’s Dilemma), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned cohort n=11, mean age 25.6, range 21–36), satisfying the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests across subjects) and provides voxelwise contrasts with coordinates and tables of activations; whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts for the healthy group are clearly described. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) that used whole-brain voxelwise analyses to compare BOLD responses during observation of social interaction video clips vs. alone and rest. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain corrected statistical maps (figures and Table 1) and contrasts clearly from the healthy sample, addressing social-related processing. Full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social task (mutual vs. averted gaze). Sample consists of healthy young adults (reported group of 8 for fMRI), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (t-statistic activation maps averaged across subjects and displayed in Figure 4) in addition to ROI analyses, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults (12 participants, ages 21–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with contrasts between conditions, thresholding details, tables of activated regions and figures showing activation—meeting requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study examines evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment—clearly social-related processing (self-conscious/moral emotions). Participants are 19 healthy adult volunteers (ages within 18–65), meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (contrasts G−N, E−N, E−G, G−E) with statistical thresholds and tables of peak coordinates and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata; PDF not provided). Abstract indicates two fMRI experiments on understanding intentions in social interaction, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, core criteria cannot be confirmed: sample characteristics and ages (I4) are not reported in the provided content, and the paper’s reporting of group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (I5) and acceptable coordinate/figure reporting (I6) cannot be verified from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the available information. Because all inclusion criteria cannot be verified and full text is unavailable, the study must be excluded pending full-text access.

This fMRI study investigates self-face recognition, a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of self (I3). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=10, mean age 26.9) meeting age and health criteria (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs other; other vs self) analyzed with FLAME and cluster correction, with tables and figures of coordinates (I5, I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-exclusion, or non-empirical issues).

This study reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy adults (n=14, ages 18.3–23.7) performing a social-related impression-formation task (people vs objects). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., person-impression > other trial types) with voxelwise thresholding and coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The paradigm clearly targets social cognitive processing (perception/understanding of others). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate perception/understanding of self (self-face recognition) — a social-related construct (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=12, right-handed males, mean age 19.36) within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and SPM results (unknown vs scrambled, familiar vs unknown, self vs familiar) with thresholding and tables/figures (I5, I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (processing anger prosody in voices), using a dichotic listening social-communication task — satisfying I3. Participants were 15 right-handed healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 24.4), and results are reported for this healthy group — satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and second-level random-effects analyses (SPM2), with coordinates and cluster-level statistics reported across the whole brain — satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is primary empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria, and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13, mean age 24.9) using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind and empathy cartoon task), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts analyzed with SPM2 using random-effects one-sample t tests and presents thresholded statistical maps and tables of activation foci (coordinates). Results for the healthy control group are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (virtual gaze and socially relevant vs arbitrary facial expressions) in healthy adults. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 25.9), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects; contrasts SOC>ARB, ARB>SOC, ME>OTHER, OTHER>ME, interactions) with stereotactic coordinates and figures/tables of activations. Results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group-only; empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study investigates detection of visuo-motor vs visuo-proprioceptive synchrony, a task probing perception and understanding of self (ownership of movement), which falls under the review’s social-related constructs. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=15 after exclusion; ages 20–28), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps and their comparison) with SPM analyses and thresholded statistical maps and tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception—a social-cognition task (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–32). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses with reported significant clusters, Talairach coordinates, t-values, and tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of group whole-brain task effects.

Full text appears incomplete (only summary/abstract-level content provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of social-related processing: face perception/understanding of others). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I4 (no information on sample demographics or confirmation of healthy adults age 18–65), I5 (no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group), I6 (format of any whole-brain results cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently applied based on available content. Because key methodological and results details are missing, the study is excluded pending full-text information.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social interactive (competitive reaction-time) task that manipulates provocation, retaliation, and observing an opponent — a clearly social-related paradigm. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (16 males; mean age 28.6), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. Imaging methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise thresholds and FDR correction; results are reported as activation maps and coordinate tables (Tables 1–3 and figures), clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the review.

The paper reports original task-based fMRI data examining social cognition (dehumanization/perception of others) using healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5, N=10 and N=12). Methods describe whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and contrast maps (subtractive analyses and 3-vs-1 contrasts) reported in the text/tables and figures. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion sections. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 29.4) who performed a social-related task (meaning-relatedness judgments of social concepts vs. animal-function concepts). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts are reported (e.g., social vs. animal; conjunction analyses) with thresholding, cluster coordinates, tables, and figures clearly derived from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods (subjects, fMRI paradigm, acquisition, analysis), results, and discussion; core article content appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (facial emotion recognition/age discrimination) relevant to perception/understanding of others; reports data from a healthy adult sample (29 adults, ages 20–35) with results for the healthy group; and presents group-level whole-brain activation results (voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps and tables/figures) clearly attributed to the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study).

The study reports an fMRI task that manipulates self-referential processing and perspective taking (social cognition), and reports group-level activations in distinct medial prefrontal cortex regions for the relevant contrasts. Participants are described as study participants (no clinical/sample-limited groups), consistent with healthy adult samples typical for this journal and design. The paper presents whole-brain task-evoked activations (contrasts for self vs. other, perspective taking, and their interaction) described in the results, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting (coordinates/activation foci are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating social communication (communicative speech) in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., communication vs description, familiar vs unfamiliar) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and provides coordinates/tables of activated regions (see Table 3 and figures). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) but the reported neuroimaging results are presented primarily as ROI-based small-volume-corrected analyses. The manuscript does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map or thresholded whole-brain results for the healthy group (only ROI SVC results and a brief mention of an exploratory V1 finding without full whole-brain statistics). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked reporting (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study manipulating social content (trustworthiness) in an n-back working memory paradigm (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22) reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and provides tables of peak voxels and clusters for main effects and interactions (Tables 2–4), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participant ages within 18–65, and is empirical).

This paper reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (empathy/perception of others’ pain), with healthy adult participants (N≈36, ages ~21) and group-level whole-brain task contrasts (painful vs non-painful) reported (pre- and post-priming whole-brain analyses, FDR-corrected). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.3) that directly investigates social/person-related processing (familiar vs. unfamiliar faces; social closeness judgments). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using random-effects GLM with voxelwise FDR correction and cluster-thresholding, and provides peak coordinates and tables of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported via coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI to probe perception of others (face gender perception—a social perception construct). (I4) The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=15 analyzed, ages 19–42). (I5/I6) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (random-effects voxel-wise analysis of gender-different > gender-same; cluster-corrected maps and coordinates are reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task activation maps).

This fMRI study investigates social conflict/resource sharing (a social-related task), uses event-related fMRI, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Conflict>No Conflict, interaction effects, conjunctions) with tables/figures and coordinates. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). Whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study examines neural correlates of abstract vs concrete mindsets using tasks that engage social-cognitive processes (mentalizing/understanding others’ actions). It reports data from healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–27). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are described (one-sample t-tests, corrected thresholds) with activation tables and figures reported. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.5) that uses a social-related task (beauty comparisons of other people) addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (conjunctions, main effects) with voxelwise thresholds and clusterwise FWE correction, tables/figures of coordinates, and ROI analyses; whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It used fMRI to decode learned social roles (pre- and post-learning face perception runs tied to a cyberball social interaction), meeting the review’s criterion for social-related fMRI (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=15, mean age ~24), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight results (random-effects SPM, FWE-corrected clusters in superior temporal sulcus with MNI coordinates and t-values), which constitute voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked maps (I5). Coordinates and inferential statistics are provided in the text/supplement, meeting I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., study does not report only ROI analyses or connectivity only). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), involving healthy adult participants (experiments: n=25, ages 19–27; n=14, ages 18–23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with statistical thresholds and tables of results and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (learning from romantic interest/rejection) using a task that is squarely social (speed-dating paradigm). Sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned group N=38, ages 19–31). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SPM8 analyses) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE control, and provides tables of activation coordinates (Tables 1–4) and figures. The full text includes Introduction, detailed Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) in healthy adults (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and coordinates (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects, tables/figures) and describes methodological details (participants, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM, thresholds, PPI). Results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social regulation (hand-holding by friend vs. stranger vs. alone) in healthy adults (mean age ~23.6). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (threat vs. safe) identified via FEAT/FLAME cluster-wise tests to define functional ROIs, and reports statistical results in tables/figures/text. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (N=18, mean age 26) that reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and coordinate-based results (CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU, etc.) with second-level random-effects analyses. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria applied: ["I3","I4","I5","I6"]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed; mean age 24.6) that used task-based fMRI during social-communicative gesture observation and imitation, addressing social communication and understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5; Monte-Carlo whole-brain cluster correction) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations (e.g., IPL, mOFC, mPFC), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adult task activations, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–45) using a social-related paradigm (viewing and regulating responses to images of human suffering), fulfilling the review’s domain. The sample consists entirely of healthy adults and results are reported for these groups. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction, whole-brain corrected at p < .01) and reports clusters (IPC, DLPFC) identified via whole-brain and conjunction analyses; these are group-level, task-evoked voxelwise results from the healthy sample. Results are described in the main text and figures, satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) using a social gambling task where participants won/lost money for self, friend, or antagonist. The study reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates, and applies small-volume FWE corrections; results are clearly from the healthy/control group. The task probes social constructs (responses to outcomes for others vs self) meeting the social-related processing scope. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining social communication/influence (message communicators) and related social-cognitive processes (mentalizing, reward). Participants are healthy adults (interns and producers; mean ages ~20) with exclusion of psychoactive medication; results report group-level, whole-brain random-effects task-evoked analyses with reported coordinates and thresholds (p < .005, k = 60) and tables/figures. The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out of range, non-empirical) apply. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’ — perception/understanding of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. Sample: 19 healthy right-handed volunteers aged 21–29, meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (what vs implicit baseline, how vs implicit baseline, how vs what) with statistical thresholds (PFWE) and tables/coordinates and figures localizing activations (e.g., right dorso-central insula). Results are clearly reported for the healthy participant group. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study investigates social cognition (theory of mind, emotion, pain attribution), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=46, ages 18–31). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate GLM second-level t-tests with cluster correction, whole-brain maps and tables) and multivoxel pattern analyses with normalized group maps. The sample is within the specified adult age range and healthy, and whole-brain results are clearly described and presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-evaluation task (being watched by a peer), reporting task-evoked whole-brain group analyses identifying MPFC activation and MPFC–striatal connectivity. The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 18–22.9) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons; coordinates and cluster statistics are provided. Although the sample spans childhood through early adulthood and the reported maps reflect the full healthy sample (not an adults-only subgroup), the inclusion criteria require at least one healthy adult group (present) and at least one whole-brain group-level map from healthy participants (present). Supplemental material is referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (N=21 healthy adult males, ages 23–33) viewed and rated dyadic nonverbal interactions while undergoing task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., meaningful videos > scrambled; main effects and interactions) with cluster-level correction and stereotactic coordinates in tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level results reported, and results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results (behavioral and neural), Discussion, and references.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1). The task is explicitly social (impression formation of real people met in person) and was performed during BOLD fMRI. Group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported (functional localizer contrast form impression > sequencing, and main task contrasts), with cluster-corrected results and tables of coordinates provided. The healthy adult group is reported separately and analyses are within-subject/group (random-effects GLM). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social perception task (passive viewing of point-light biological motion), reporting results for healthy adult participants (n=48, ages 20–35). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (biological > scrambled motion) and Sex×Condition ANOVAs, with figures and tables of whole-brain results and cluster-corrected thresholds. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 19–28) that investigates social-related processing (implicit/explicit detection of social signals and implicit mental-state inference). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and lists activation peaks (tables/figures) and describes voxelwise statistical thresholds and cluster-corrections. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of third-party punishment (social cognition: perception/understanding of others/mentalizing) using a task during scanning. The sample includes 26 healthy adult participants (age 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects GLM, whole-brain FDR q<0.05) with peak coordinates and described activations (R TPJ, R anterior insula). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing traffic-awareness videos eliciting socio-cognitive processes; CV vs NV), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adult participants (male, ages ~19–30), meeting I4 (ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (within-group CV vs NV contrasts and whole-brain maps illustrated in Fig.1; and tables/coordinates for clusters), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported, ages within range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of face processing (faces vs diverse objects), which constitutes social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others) and thus meets I3. The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 18–37) and all participants are healthy, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and maps (faces>objects contrast; Table 3 and whole-brain figures), meeting I5 and I6. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical limitations). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This full-text article reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (attribute framing and self/other perspective-taking), meeting the review’s scope. The sample consists of healthy adults (ages 19–41; N recruited = 21, with exclusions reported), satisfying the adult healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., task vs control, positive minus negative frame, negative minus positive frame, frame-inconsistent minus frame-consistent) with coordinate results and thresholding details, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence criterion. Whole-brain results are described in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used task-based fMRI to evaluate social judgments (approachability of faces), a social cognition construct. The abstract and methods/references indicate group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (reporting activation in left amygdala and frontal gyri, SPM and cluster-thresholding references), and the sample appears to be healthy adult participants with trait anxiety measured. However, the provided full text is incomplete (paywall/partial content), so I cannot fully verify participant ages and the exact presentation of unmasked healthy-group whole-brain maps. Inclusion is supported by the available information but confidence is reduced due to incomplete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-affective processing (empathic judgments/EEB) using task-based fMRI. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (female undergraduates) in the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (interaction contrasts) with coordinates and figures (fMRI1 whole-brain exploratory; fMRI2 with SVC but also a whole-brain analysis reported), satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps are available (coordinates/figures). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Dynamic Social Gesture task) in healthy participants. The sample comprises young adults (mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7) with the majority within 18–65; results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (TFCE with permutation testing) and presents whole-brain results in figures and tables. Reporting of whole-brain maps/coordinates is clear. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range-only samples, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the review of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a social task (collaborative vs competitive interactions) during functional MRI and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (SPMs, clusterwise FWE-corrected maps and tables). Sample: healthy adults (n=32; ages 18–39) meeting the age and health requirements. Whole-brain GLM analyses and SPM results are reported and described in the text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not an only between-group contrast, participants are within the 18–65 range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–39) that uses task-based fMRI while participants made social judgments of ambiguous interactions (social coordination), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, FDR-corrected contrasts; results presented in figures and tables), meeting the whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. The healthy adult sample falls within the 18–65 range. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; it appears complete.

This paper is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study relating gray matter volumes to proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults. It does not report task-evoked fMRI group-level whole-brain activation maps from the healthy/control group. Although it references prior fMRI work and uses a subgroup’s SSC-BOLD values as covariates, it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, task-evoked healthy-group fMRI statistical map required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use functional MRI during a social-related task as the primary reported modality) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked fMRI map reported for the healthy group). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) explicitly apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from the fMRI task-activation meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (live verbal communication/social interaction), includes a healthy adult sample (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (talking, listening, imagining) with voxelwise t-tests and cluster-correction; results are presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This study reports task-based fMRI of explicit social judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli (I3). The sample comprises 44 healthy adults aged 21–60, within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (random-effects ANOVA) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and reports peak coordinates and figures (satisfying I5 and I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 34), using task-based fMRI during naturalistic social stimuli. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results and multiple voxelwise contrasts (including conjunction analyses) with coordinates and figures, and describes preprocessing and statistical methods. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as contrasts/coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, age range appropriate, and empirical original data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI task study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) in healthy adults (male participants aged 18–40). The methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5) with voxelwise contrasts, cluster-thresholding, and coordinate results/figures for main effects and interactions—satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task clearly probes social-related processes via perspective-taking instructions and sad/neutral emotional contexts. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (one-shot prisoner’s dilemma), directly probing social cognition/understanding of others (meets I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (n≈35 analyzed, mean age 24.6) within 18–65 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (contrasts, cluster-size correction, tables/figures with coordinates and statistical maps described in text), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical issues).

This article is a non-empirical review (publication type: Review; article in Japanese) that summarizes fMRI and PET research rather than reporting original fMRI data from a healthy adult sample. No methods, participant groups, or group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for healthy adults are provided in the available full-text/abstract. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review). Inclusion criteria are not met: it does not present an original fMRI social-task study in healthy adults (I3 not met), does not report a healthy adult sample (I4 not met), and does not report group-level whole-brain task activation maps/results (I5/I6 not met). Full text appears incomplete for extraction of empirical details (no methods/results present), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing partners/children/friends vs matched unfamiliar faces) that probes social cognition (affiliation/attachment, perception of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts for the healthy control group (e.g., partner>unfamiliar: left posterior cingulate, left pSTS; p<.05 FWE cluster-corrected) with coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (13 volunteers, mean age 64.5±5.7); although older, they are a healthy adult group reported separately from the clinical case and thus satisfy the ‘healthy adults’ criterion. The study also reports behavioral and SCR data, and presents mixed-effects fMRI analyses and PPI results but not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria applied: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria applied: []. Overall, the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion as an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (ultimatum game), includes a clearly reported healthy adult group (young adults 19–28) with group-level analyses, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (unfair–fair offers) with group-level one-sample t-tests, maps and tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of online social interaction (free imitation), conducted in healthy adult participants (female, 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results from GLM contrasts (imitating, being imitated, observation) with voxelwise correction (FWE/FDR) and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Although the study also reports seed-based PPI connectivity analyses, it also provides unmasked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural social touch (being touched by another person), addressing social-related processing. Participants were healthy adults (n=8, ages 22–39). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain spatial maps derived from group ICA (thresholded at z=2.5) and identifies task-related independent components whose time courses are analyzed relative to stimulus blocks; these group-average ICA maps are whole-brain voxelwise maps clearly linked to the task and reported for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-related maps), and I6 (maps/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (a social perceptual process) in healthy adults. The fMRI methods describe a task-based faces-versus-houses paradigm, second-level (group) whole-brain analysis using SPM8, and report significant group activations (tables and figures) including whole-brain clusters (p<0.05 FWE) and voxelwise suprathreshold counts in bilateral fusiform gyri. The sample includes healthy adult participants (fMRI subset N=22; mean age ~18.9) with results reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain task-evoked group results are clearly described and presented. Therefore the study satisfies the review inclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, ages 20–28) that includes social distance trials (friends vs acquaintances) constituting a social-related task. The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise searchlight MVPA and representational similarity analyses, aligned maps to standard space, tested group-level statistics against chance with FDR correction, and report clusters and tables of significant voxels (group-level whole-brain results). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

The study includes an fMRI social task (social closeness task) and reports healthy adult participants (adults aged 19–30 present), so it meets I3 and I4. However, the fMRI results are reported using ROI-based analyses (beta weights extracted from anatomically defined ROIs and SVC on VBM-derived ROIs) and no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self and peer evaluations) using a task paradigm (evaluative perspectives across social/academic/physical domains) involving both early adolescents and a healthy adult group (ages 22–31). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (a 2×4×3 whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA) and describes/selects clusters from those analyses; separate within-age-group analyses (including adult results) are referenced and reported in Supplementary Materials (tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult whole-brain task effect. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses to witnessing an emergency (a social situation), thus addressing social-related processing. Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–27), and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, parametric and contrast maps) with cluster- and FDR-corrected thresholds; results are presented in tables and figures. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=28; age 30–50) that explicitly manipulates social stimulus processing (social vs non-social pictures) within a task and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (main effects, conjunctions, specific contrasts) analyzed with SPM8 and thresholded/reported in MNI-space. This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) assessing neural responses to social rejection and relating them to romantic relationship satisfaction. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~21) using a social perception task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions with disgust). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (2×2 ANOVA and interaction contrasts), with coordinates and cluster results, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-content task (valence classification of agentic vs. communal trait words). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (agentic vs. fixation, communal vs. fixation, conjunction, and direct contrasts) with statistical correction and tables/figures, clearly from the healthy participant group (ages 18–25). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (speech act understanding: Naming vs Requesting) in healthy adults. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention), involving healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23). This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) and tests effects of personality on social versus nonsocial gesture processing (meets I3). The sample is described as healthy young adults (mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7), i.e., primarily adult participants and reported as a healthy group (meets I4). The study provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and reports cluster coordinates and figures from the healthy participant group (meets I5 and I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (explicit control of interpersonal trust/distrust) using a task performed during fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, trust+distrust > age) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures listing coordinates and clusters. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–27) using a social-interaction paradigm (perceived live vs recorded speech). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (N=20, healthy adults age 18–27) performed a task explicitly eliciting thoughts about others’ mental states (mentalizing), meeting the review’s social-related task criterion. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, analyzed N=26; ages 19–37) that uses task-based fMRI to study social learning about others’ generosity. This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (affective theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (n=22 recruited, 21 analyzed; mean age 23.73), using a task that manipulates emotional facial expressions during ToM judgments. This is an empirical fMRI study investigating processing of empathic vs. unempathic social responses (a social cognition / social communication task). This paper reports an fMRI experiment using naturalistic social-evaluative videos (E.Vids) to probe processing of positive, negative, and neutral social evaluation.
