Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma assessing cooperation) addressing social processing (I3); the sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age ~21, within 18–65) with results reported for the healthy group (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with voxel coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (e.g., CC vs. other outcomes, context contrasts) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5); and whole-brain results are presented in text/tables (MNI coordinates), acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain contrasts). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented an explicit social cognition task (valence judgments of naturalistic social interactions) during BOLD fMRI (meets I3). The sample comprises a healthy adult group (n=38, ages 18–30) with results reported for that group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (full-factorial ANOVA, whole-brain FWE-corrected results; Table 1 and figures) and reports coordinates and cluster-level results (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts; the full text includes methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text reports an fMRI reappraisal task using angry faces (socially relevant stimuli) in healthy adults (N=60; age range 18–57) and includes detailed methods, results, and discussion. The paper presents multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase vs Observe-angry; Observe-angry > Increase+Decrease) with cluster correction and tables of peaks, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Resting-state analyses are reported in addition, but task-based whole-brain results are present. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=31, ages 19–32) that used a social/prosocial reinforcement-learning task during fMRI. It reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (flexible factorial) and provides coordinates and statistical maps/tables (main effects and contrasts reported, with results presented in main text and SI tables/figures). The paper thus meets the meta-analysis objectives and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy sample. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI reference to tables/figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adults. Sample: n=32 healthy adults (female, mean age 22.7), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (Mentalizing > baseline; Empathy Task ANOVA; contrasts reported with cluster-level correction and MNI coordinates/tables), not ROI-only results. Whole-brain coordinates and tables are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: it used task-based fMRI while participants made social judgments about friends and kin (meets I3). The sample comprises 25 healthy adult females (mean age 23.2), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (friend > kin, parametric network-layer effects) with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations (meets I5 and I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages in range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study uses task-based fMRI during a Face Matching Task (implicit emotional face perception), which qualifies as social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 25), meeting the age and healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests with reported contrasts and thresholding) and refers to results presented in tables/figures (including supplementary material), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Although the paper also performs ICA connectivity analyses, it additionally provides univariate task-evoked whole-brain maps for the healthy group. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is noted but not required. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, seed/connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment manipulating social competition during a memory task (social comparison/mentalizing), uses healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35, N=20 analyzed), and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (e.g., Competition > No Competition contrasts, working-memory parametric modulators) with reported peak coordinates and cluster-correction details. The paper provides full methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), and discussion. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social communication/social language (mentalizing, social sharing) during an explicit product-recommendation task, satisfying the review’s social-related fMRI requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=19, mean age 20.55), meeting the age and health inclusion criteria. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (parametric whole-brain searches for ‘social language in’ and ‘social language out’ with cluster thresholds and tables of coordinates), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement and acceptable reporting formats. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (including whole-brain and ROI analyses), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (emotion recognition and gaze integration), meeting the review objective. It reports task-based fMRI during a social-related emotion/gaze task (I3). It includes a healthy younger adult group (ages reported 17–27, mean 20.65) analyzed separately, providing a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (PLS) and reports peak coordinates/tables and figures for these effects from the healthy groups (I5, I6). The full manuscript (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related empathy-for-pain task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, males aged 18–40). The paper reports whole-brain analyses, but the reported whole-brain voxelwise results in the full text are primarily between-group contrasts (STRESS > CONTROL and conjunctions) rather than an unmasked, within-group or main-effect whole-brain task map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The inclusion requirement I5 requires at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group; that map is not explicitly reported in the provided full text. Therefore this paper reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Exclusion rationale: E4 met; Inclusion met: I3, I4, I6 satisfied; Inclusion not met: I5 (no explicit whole-brain healthy-group task map).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16–17 for task analyses; ages 21–46) that investigates social cognition (attribution of emotions to humans and animals). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Emotion > Expression in the Explicit Task; Face > Scramble in the Implicit Task) with whole-brain analyses and cluster-level FWE correction, and presents whole-brain results in text, figures, and supplementary tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The provided content (abstract, highlights, metadata) indicates an fMRI study of emotional face perception in 40 healthy adult volunteers, satisfying inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), so I cannot verify that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I5). Without access to the full methods/results, I cannot confirm whole-brain results versus ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract alone. Because I5 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text access.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants performed emotion (positive vs negative) and age judgments on dynamic face videos (social perception of others). Sample: healthy adults aged 21–33 (final N=25), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses: a whole-brain univariate random-effects faces>objects contrast to define ROIs, and whole-brain searchlight MVPA with SnPM correction and reported clusters/coordinates (Table 3 and figures), indicating task-evoked, group-level whole-brain statistical maps for the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used task-based functional MRI to assess social interaction recognition (social-related processing) (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SI > NM) for the adult group with voxelwise/statistical results and cluster/FWE correction described (I5), and whole-brain results are presented in text/figures/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, are not only connectivity or resting-state analyses, and adult whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, and discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) that explicitly investigates social-related processing (self-related processing, mentalizing/social cognition) during a task presenting news headlines/abstracts. The manuscript describes group-level whole-brain analyses (see SI whole-brain analyses, Fig. S3 and Table S5) and reports corrected voxelwise/cluster thresholds and permutation testing, indicating at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map derived from the healthy participant samples. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides ROI and whole-brain results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.  Confidence is high given explicit reporting of whole-brain group analyses and clear healthy adult samples.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using task-based scans to probe person-knowledge retrieval (a social cognition task: perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM results and contrasts (e.g., all memory > baseline; status > baseline; face > name) thresholded and reported with coordinates and SPM maps (univariate analyses, supplementary figures/tables). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages within 18–65). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) using a social/mentalising task (theory-of-mind/mentalising questions vs factual questions), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 22 years, within 18–65). The paper describes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2), reports contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation), thresholding and cluster-correction procedures, and provides a Table of significant whole‑brain results and rendered maps; neuroimaging data are also linked (DOI). The full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core article content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is an fMRI investigation of social action-outcome contingency (telling jokes and hearing listener laughter), addressing social processing/self-related and reward networks. It reports task-based whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (multiple one-sample/random-effects analyses, interaction effects, and SPM maps with cluster-level FWE correction) explicitly from a healthy adult sample (n=38, ages 19–29). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (decisions to share vs select news articles; social-cognition and self-related processing constructs). Sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–24 (N=41 analyzed). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction (p < .05, k > 20) and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes an appropriate healthy adult group, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making: participants performed a social/spatial decision task while fMRI was acquired (neuroimaging cohort described). The neuroimaging sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (neuroimaging subset n=62, ages 18–53). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (e.g., activation maps in Fig. 7C, Supplementary Tables, multiple-comparisons correction via SnPM) and provides NeuroVault links for statistical maps. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–30) using a social task (modified Trust Game) probing reciprocity and social decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, cluster-corrected voxelwise results, coordinate tables/figures) for the healthy participant sample and describes univariate whole-brain activation results and ICA-derived network analyses. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants performed an explicit social-related task (mental simulation of personally familiar people in contexts). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=25 recruited; 23 analyzed; ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and random-effects t-test results with correction for multiple comparisons and displays whole-brain maps/tables (Figures and Table 1). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group results.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) while participants observed others’ social-integrity threats, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample: N=34 healthy adult males aged 19–31 (within 18–65), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SIT > NEUT) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, age range acceptable, empirical primary data present). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of implicit/explicit theory-of-mind (social cognition: perception and understanding of others) in healthy adults (mean age 24.4, N=22 analyzed), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports a whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) with voxelwise results (q[FDR]<0.05) and reported peak Talairach coordinates and an activation image, fulfilling the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group. The implicit task analyses used ROIs derived from that whole-brain localizer but the presence of the whole-brain localizer prevents exclusion under ROI-only rules. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete.

This study uses fMRI during a social task (theory-of-mind stories) with healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the full text presents ROI-based MVPA analyses and ROI definition procedures (using first-level Belief>Photo contrasts) but does not clearly report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group in the main text provided. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-based results without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map, it fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI task examining neural responses to romantic and sexual stimuli (social/affiliation-related processing). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 22–50). The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME random effects, cluster correction) and the Results present group-level whole-brain contrasts (e.g., sexual > neutral for all participants; romantic > neutral and within-group contrasts), with tables and figures reporting activations. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical limitations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This empirical fMRI study uses task-based fMRI to investigate implicit attitudes and executive control in the context of romantic attachment/interest in extra-pair relationships (social/affiliation/attachment domain). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (27 males, ages 20–32). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (IAT incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides peak coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (perception of third-party social interactions) using task-based BOLD imaging (I3). Sample comprises 14 healthy adults aged 20–32 with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., interaction > independent contrast, MNI coordinates, group maps and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5/I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social perception/evaluation (impression-formation of faces varying in race and socioeconomic status), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises 60 healthy adult (White) men (Mage=23.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain regressions targeting status and reported clusters, voxelwise thresholding and a whole-brain VMPFC cluster shown in Figure 4 and Supplementary Material S4). Whole-brain results are reported in the text/figure/supplement, satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study that probes social-related perception (judging potential for social involvement from point-light and human-like walkers), meeting the review objective. Participants are healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (second-level fMRI analyses) and provides stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding details (FWE-corrected, cluster/peak) in tables and figures, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; tabulated coordinates and described contrasts are acceptable per I6. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study used fMRI to examine responses to attachment-related narratives in healthy adults and reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity (FC) changes after listening. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study addressing a social-related construct: attachment/affiliation) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map from the healthy/control group is reported). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (the paper reports only seed-based resting-state FC analyses and does not provide a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis which requires task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social/communicative memory in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–33). The task explicitly probes social communication/collaboration (collaboratively vs. individually learned labels), and authors report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results and tables/figures) and an ROI follow-up; whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=36 healthy adults, ages within 18–65) observed social interactions varying in cooperativity and affectivity. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; cluster-level FDR-corrected maps and tables/figures) showing activations and parametric effects, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. It also includes DCM effective-connectivity analyses, but these are supplemental to and accompany whole-brain task activation results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social joint action (haptic leading/following/mutual), meeting the review focus on social-related processing. Participants: healthy adults (n=18 analyzed; mean age 40.4), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (partnered vs. non-partnered; improvisation contrasts) with Talairach coordinates and tables, and corrected/statistical maps described in the text, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that tests human perception and neural responses to affective vocalisations (a social-communication task). Sample: healthy adults (N=19, mean age 25.9) meeting the age and health requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task analyses (species contrast human > chimpanzee > macaque) with statistical images and MNI coordinates (Table 2, Fig. 2), and describes preprocessing and mixed-effects group analysis (FLAME). Results are reported as whole-brain effects and coordinates (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports task-based fMRI of social processing (Theory of Mind: TOM vs Random contrast) in a large sample of healthy adults (HCP n=787; ages reported within 22–>35, so within 18–65). The authors generated and analyzed group-level whole-brain task statistical maps (level-2 cope files and level-3 z maps from HCP, transformed into group Cohen's d maps) and present group activation maps/figures and cluster tables derived from the healthy participant group. Results are reported at the group level and include voxelwise maps/visualizations (figures and supplementary material), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (self/friend/celebrity social-role judgments). The sample consists of 37 healthy male adults (mean age 22.9), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (self vs. celebrity, friend vs. celebrity) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/coordinates, and describes these healthy-group task effects in the text and figures. Although the study also reports gPPI connectivity results, these are supplemental to the primary whole-brain task activations rather than being the sole reported results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–38) using a social decision-making task (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction, COMP>COOP, time-course analyses) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures describing activations and contrasts, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly contrasts social vs. non-social stimuli. It meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing: social vs. non-social image appraisal), I4 (healthy adult sample ages 23–50, N=14 analyzed), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain social>non-social contrast with thresholded maps and cluster tables), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion perception (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–24). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and contrasts) with PFWE-corrected results and tables/figures, meeting the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group activation maps. The sample is healthy adults and results are reported for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

Only title/abstract/metadata provided; full text (methods, results, figures, tables) is not available, so I cannot verify reporting of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps required by I5. The abstract confirms fMRI during a social decision task (I3) and healthy participants (I4), but does not state whether whole-brain task activation results for the healthy group are reported (and emphasizes functional connectivity), so inclusion criteria I5/I6 cannot be confirmed. Therefore exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailability preventing verification of required whole-brain results.

Only the article abstract is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates an fMRI study of social communicative prosody, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, the sample details (ages and health status) required for I4 are not reported in the abstract, and there is no verification that whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps are reported (I5/I6). Because the full text (methods/results/tables) is not available, I cannot confirm whole-brain results or participant age range. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Recommend obtaining the complete full text to verify I4 and I5 before inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation of the self), conducted in a healthy adult sample (n=31, ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem as a regressor, with coordinates, tables, and figures, and appropriate statistical thresholds. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation (intelligence and friendliness from faces) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–28), so it meets I3 and I4. However, the analysis was restricted to prespecified ROIs (search regions restricted to amygdala, insula, IFG, ACC, thalamus, caudate, mOFC) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. The paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or maps for the healthy group, only ROI-restricted results; therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly I3 and I4 are satisfied; I5 is not met; exclusion E2 applies.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study that includes a social cognition task (social interaction vs. random movement) analyzed with task contrasts and psychophysiological interactions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants from HCP and UCLA (ages within 21–50 and 22–36+), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper describes voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and presents group-level task activation results (e.g., Figures and voxel-wise GLM methods), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps; results are reported in the main text and figures. The study is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and is an empirical report with original fMRI data. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This randomized, double-blind within-subject fMRI study tested 55 healthy adult males (mean age 24.9) during a social task (erotic and fearful social scenes), fulfilling the review’s focus on social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., erotic vs. neutral; fearful vs. neutral; erotic vs. fearful) with p < 0.05 FWE-corrected results and ROI results; whole-brain findings are described in the text and supplementary material. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults: (a) it used task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (mind perception and gaze-cueing) (meets I3); (b) sample = 22 healthy adults (mean age 24.36) within 18–65 (meets I4); (c) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses with family-wise error / cluster correction and tables/figures describing whole-brain results (vmPFC and other regions) (meets I5); (d) whole-brain results are presented in text, figures and tables (meets I6). Full text (methods, results, discussion, tables, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (emotional face recognition of own vs. unknown child), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without ELM and without lifetime mental disorder), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results: within-group whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected) are reported for the control group (e.g., familiarity effect own>unknown in medial frontal gyrus with coordinates and pFWE values), satisfying I5. Results and maps/coordinates are reported in tables/figures, satisfying I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are adults, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=35) using a social-related task (recall of autobiographical relationship episodes involving self and others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with FDR-corrected cluster inference and provides tables/figures of results. Healthy adult sample is reported and analyzed as a group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-out-of-range, or non-empirical paper issues). Full text appears complete (not truncated).

Full text inaccessible (404 Not Found). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not available, so I cannot verify whether the study used task-based fMRI targeting social processing in healthy adults or reported whole-brain group-level results. Title suggests relevance, but without the full text I cannot confirm I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), or I6 (location of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 can be confirmed either. Therefore the study is excluded due to incomplete full text preventing assessment of all inclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study examines audiovisual integration of emotional face and voice expressions (a social communication/perception task) in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 26). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE-corrected results, conjunctions, and coordinates, and presents whole-brain figures and tables; results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), satisfying I3. The sample includes a younger healthy adult group aged 20–33, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (ANOVA, figures, and Supplementary Table for whole-brain analyses), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), and include within-group/whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E4). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (N=28 analyzed; ages 18–22). The task involves mentalizing about others' mental states (social-related constructs). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (searchlight RSA and repetition suppression with permutation TFCE correction) with reported corrected clusters (medial PFC, precuneus) and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-related maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and visualized). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no only connectivity/resting-state, no only between-group contrasts, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) performed during functional MRI, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (FWE cluster-corrected maps and tables of activations). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=20 males, age range 21–37) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (main effects and treatment×opponent interactions) and tables/figures of activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (age 18–22) using a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) with task-evoked BOLD fMRI. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholding, cluster correction) and presents whole-brain results in the text/tables/figures for the healthy sample (and for subgroups). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not outside age range, not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a validated social-provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adult males aged 18–35 (n=93 after exclusions), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (high>low provocation) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides MNI coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present, and no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, subgroup-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical dual‑fMRI (task-based) hyperscanning study of social interaction (adapted pattern game) that measures task‑evoked BOLD responses modulated by partners’ behavior, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 44 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.37), meeting I4. The paper reports group‑level, whole‑brain random‑effects analyses (FLAME) with non‑parametric permutation correction and presents cluster tables and thresholded whole‑brain maps (Tables/Figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI‑only, connectivity/resting‑state only, between‑group‑only contrasts, out‑of‑range age, or non‑empirical paper) apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

Full text not provided (only title/abstract/metadata). From the abstract the study uses fMRI of a social-related task (interpersonal pleasant touch) — I3 satisfied. The sample includes a healthy control group (non-using controls), but ages (18–65) are not reported in the abstract so I4 cannot be confirmed. Crucially, the abstract does not confirm whether group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation maps are reported (I5); this cannot be verified without the full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm required whole-brain reporting and thus must exclude pending full-text review.

Full text content is incomplete (only title/metadata available). Cannot verify required inclusion criteria: I3 (uncertain whether a social-related task fMRI was used vs. resting-state), I4 (uncertain whether a healthy adult control group is included and reported separately), I5 (no evidence of whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for healthy/control group), I6 (no information on how results are reported). No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available material. Because core inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract confirms task-based fMRI of a social cognition construct (theory of mind), so I3 is met. However, the paper primarily reports resting-state/intrinsic connectivity results, and the abstract does not specify any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps from a healthy adult group (I5 not confirmed). Participant age ranges are not provided in the abstract, so I4 (at least one healthy adult group aged 18–65) cannot be confirmed. Because the full text is not available, I cannot verify whole-brain task activation reporting or disambiguate whether task-evoked healthy-group maps are presented (I5, I6). Therefore the study must be excluded at this stage pending full-text access. No exclusion criteria from the list are definitively met based on the abstract alone.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract, highlights, and metadata provided). I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: dynamic facial expression perception/imagery) is satisfied based on the abstract. However I4 (explicit report of a healthy adult sample, ages 18–65) cannot be confirmed from the provided content, and I5 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group) cannot be verified because methods/results and group-level maps or coordinates are not present. I6 (acceptability of whole-brain results in tables/figures) likewise cannot be assessed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available text. Recommend obtaining the full manuscript (methods and results) to assess participant sample and presence of whole-brain healthy-group task maps before inclusion.

This study uses fMRI in healthy adult participants and investigates perception/recognition of faces (social perception), but the full text reports ROI-based MVPA and representational analyses across predefined face and visual-field ROIs. It does not present or describe any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures clearly identified as whole-brain healthy-group activation—only ROI and ROI-based regression results are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face perception/recognition task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social interactions (live bidirectional conversations human–human and human–robot), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 25.8, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM analyses, cluster-level FDR-corrected contrasts such as HHI vs HRI; figures and NeuroVault/OpenNeuro repositories provided). Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and described in the text. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure toward human and robot agents) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task analyses (cluster-corrected results and whole-brain maps; NeuroVault link provided) and provides coordinates/tables for whole-brain contrasts. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described/tabled/archived). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of co-speech gestures/social communication in healthy adults. The paper reports a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task analysis (SPM second-level, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures, and details of methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (ages 22–35). The task relates to social communication/perception (co-speech gesture integration) which maps onto the review’s social-related constructs. No exclusion criteria appear to be triggered.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) that includes a healthy adult control group, but the manuscript does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper reports between-group contrasts (BPD > HC, NSSI > HC) and a conjunction of these contrasts, but no within-group HC whole-brain activation map (social inclusion > passive watching) is presented or described as a standalone, unmasked healthy-group effect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map not reported).

The study used task-based fMRI to investigate perception of animacy from visual motion—an instance of social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–36) and fMRI results are reported for the healthy groups (random-effects, group-level whole-brain analyses with voxelwise FWE correction; whole-brain maps and cluster coordinates are described and plotted). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion (complete full text provided). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports fMRI data from 78 healthy adults (age 18–40) and includes multiple clearly social-related tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, vocalizations). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects (RFX) analyses and t maps (voxelwise p<0.05 FWE-corrected) and provides detailed methods and results for the healthy cohort. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI social-task requirement, healthy-adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=51 healthy adults, age mean 22.5) that investigates processing of dynamic facial expressions—a social communication/perception task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (dynamic expressions vs dynamic mosaics) using random-effects analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds, with statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, tables).

Excluded because exclusion criteria E2 and E3 are met: the paper reports only ROI/parcellation-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network analyses (Power-264 ROIs, nodal/global network metrics and interregional FC) and does not present any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — vocal emotional processing/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample, N=36, ages 20–35). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (trust/honesty) using task-based fMRI (TAG and subsequent trust game). Sample: 31 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.29), within 18–65, reported and analyzed as a healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (multiple GLMs, whole-brain contrasts, cluster- and voxel-level FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates and figures) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Whole-brain results are described in the main text and Supplementary Tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=13, mean age 26.6; Experiment 2: n=18, mean age 23.1) that investigates social-relevant vocal versus non-vocal sound processing (social communication/perception). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (vocal > non-vocal; thresholded voxelwise, FDR corrected, cluster thresholds) and describes whole-brain ICA/time-frequency analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I6 (maps reported in figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

Full-text reports task-based fMRI during observation of social touch (social-related processing), includes a healthy neurotypical adult control group (21 NT adults) with results reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (group contrasts and tables/coordinates in main/supplementary files). The full article contains methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study probing social-related processing: it tests how collective (social) schemas influence individual memory and shows dmPFC/vmPFC representations linked to collective/social knowledge (mentalizing, narratives). Sample: 24 healthy adult participants (ages 22–39), satisfying the healthy adult group requirement. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (surface-based searchlight, TFCE-corrected results; Extended Data Fig.1 and whole-brain searchlight methods/results are described), providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).
